title: reserved-pool-autoscaler-misallocation-and-burst-cap-shortage
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden throughput collapse on Dedicated reserved pools during daily peak. Root cause traced to autoscaler miscomputing available burst capacity when multiple allocation windows overlapped, which allowed the scheduler to overcommit GPUs and then artificially fail new allocations until manual intervention. This ticket captures the investigation, fix, rollout, and immediate remediation steps (hotfix + follow-up work).
timeline: 2026-02-20 09:12 - Alert from PagerDuty: reserved-pool 'eu-west-2-prod-1' showing allocation failures and dropped requests. Initial MTTD ~6m.
2026-02-20 09:28 - Customer support (CS-9821) escalated: three customers (AcmeHealth, FinLedger, RetailScale) reported increased 429/503 spike and SLA violations.
2026-02-20 09:35 - Triage call with on-call infra, runtime, and capacity teams. Repro steps started against staging with traffic replay.
2026-02-20 10:05 - Preliminary hypothesis: autoscaler calculation uses stale KV-cache TTL for burst headroom leading to double-counting reserved headroom during overlapping scale decisions.

2026-02-20 11:20 - Mitigation 1: Reduced autoscaler aggressiveness by halving max-scale step for all Dedicated pools globally; applied via remote config (feature flag: autoscaler.step-limit=0.5). Immediate drop in failed allocations but latency increased for some queued requests.
2026-02-20 12:15 - Hotfix branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8276 - fixes ordering bug where burst_headroom was applied both pre- and post-allocation check.
2026-02-20 15:40 - Hotfix deployed to eu-west-2 canary after QA smoke: allocation success rate returned to baseline for canary pool.
2026-02-20 17:00 - Global rollout plan executed with coordinated customer comms. All impacted customers notified of progress and timelines.
2026-02-21 09:00 - Post-deploy monitoring: 24h window shows no recurrence in affected pools. Marked incident mitigated but follow-ups required.

2026-02-25 10:30 - Root-cause analysis completed: race condition in autoscaler decision path (allocator/main.go) where cached available_vram metric could be updated concurrently by a background reconciler, leading to a negative available capacity being clamped incorrectly and then persisted for the duration of the reconciliation window.

2026-02-28 14:00 - Additional fixes merged: stronger invariants added, integration test that replays concurrent reconciler + allocation events, and metrics for 'autoscaler_overcommit_attempts' and 'autoscaler_unavailable_clamps'. PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8290, github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8311.
2026-03-05 09:45 - Customer retrospective calls scheduled; action items assigned for billing adjustments and SLA credits where appropriate.
2026-03-10 16:20 - This ticket moved to In Review for final sign-off on runbook updates and backfill tests before closing.
2026-03-10 16:25 - Follow-up work queued: graceful backoff prioritization for high-value customers during pool stress (ENG-15322) and autoscaler chaos-testing harness (ENG-15323).
resolution: Fix implemented in runtime-2.4.1: reorder evaluation so burst_headroom is applied only after computing stable available_vram and before commit; add atomic snapshotting of capacity metrics during allocation decision to avoid race-state; clamp logic adjusted to prefer conservative non-blocking fallback (route to lower priority pool) instead of hard-failing allocations. Added integration tests and a dedicated metric suite to detect similar regressions early.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator ordering and clamp logic (added)
- Integration test that replays overlapping reconciler and allocation events (added)
- Canary rollout to single EU region for 24h with synthetic load mirroring customers' 95th percentile traffic
- Full global rollout with observability dashboard (link below) and alert thresholds tightened for 'autoscaler_overcommit_attempts'>0
customer_communications: 2026-02-20 18:00 - Initial customer notification sent explaining that we identified a scaling coordination bug and applied a mitigant; promised follow-up after root cause analysis.
2026-02-21 11:00 - Update: Hotfix deployed; customers asked to validate traffic patterns and confirm reduction in errors; support conference calls scheduled separately.
2026-03-06 15:30 - Final postmortem and SLA credit conversation with affected accounts; ops committed to improving burst observability and providing quarterly capacity reviews.
open_questions: Should we introduce a soft quota per-customer inside a reserved pool to reduce blast radius for noisy tenants?
What is the target detection lead time for 'autoscaler_unavailable_clamps' before we consider automated rollback? Current threshold: 5m. Is 1m reasonable?
Do we need per-pool canary scaling windows (staggered schedules) to avoid simultaneous reconciler update storms?
next_steps: ENG-15322: Implement prioritized fallback routing so high-value customers are routed to alternate pools with graceful degradation (assignee: Priya Desai).
ENG-15323: Add autoscaler chaos-testing harness to CI that introduces reconciler delays and concurrent allocation spikes (assignee: Omar Rahman).
Update runbook to include new mitigation knobs and step-by-step manual recovery for reserved-pool depletion (owner: Miguel Ortega).
Schedule quarterly capacity review with top 10 Dedicated customers and include burst headroom recommendations (owner: Aisha Khan).
